title: Delete the sets completely
description:
Given the sets `A = {19, 22, 24, 20, 25, 26}` and `B = {19, 22, 20, 25, 26, 24, 28, 27}`: Delete the sets completely.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `clear_set(s)`, emptying the given set completely (leaving zero elements) and returning a SORTED list of its (now empty) contents.
hints: Emptying a set entirely is different from removing one element at a time - there's a single method that wipes out everything at once.
Sets have a method, shared with lists and dictionaries, that removes every element and leaves the collection empty in place.
Call the set's .clear() method, then return sorted(s), which will be an empty list.
expected_behavior: Removes every element from the given set and returns a sorted list of what remains (always an empty list).
explanation: set.clear() removes every element from the set in place, leaving it empty but still a valid set object - this is how you delete a set's contents completely without deleting the variable itself.
